core_principles: Narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) elicit higher triceps brachii activation compared to traditional shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP).
Narrow-width push-ups can be utilized as a more advanced variation of the traditional push-up to offer a greater training challenge.
specific_findings: The study analyzed one healthy male gymnastic participant (age = 25 years, weight = 65 kg) performing five repetitions of each variation.
Narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) elicited triceps brachii EMG activity of 5.11 ± 1.97 mV and 105.83 ± 18.54 %MVC.
Shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP) produced triceps brachii EMG values of 3.91 ± 1.36 mV and 74.32 ± 16.9 %MVC.

core_principles: Hand positioning significantly impacts muscle recruitment and exercise difficulty during push-ups.
Narrow-base push-ups (NWPP) recruit the triceps brachii to a greater degree and enhance shoulder stability.
Shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP) increase activation of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid, supporting general chest and shoulder strength.
specific_findings: Mankowski et al. (2016) compared narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups over a 12-week training period, finding narrow-based push-ups elicited greater triceps brachii activation while shoulder-width showed higher activation in the pectoralis major.

Jang et al. (2019) found that narrow-based push-ups led to significantly higher activation of the triceps brachii, while shoulder-width push-ups showed increased activation of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid among elite gymnasts.

core_principles: Select narrow-based push-ups to isolate and recruit the triceps and anterior deltoids, and to build endurance in the rotator cuff and shoulder stabilizers.
Select shoulder-width push-ups to target the pectoralis major and overall chest musculature for a more balanced upper-body workout.
Utilize shoulder-width push-ups to maintain better postural control and reduce the risk of improper alignment, especially during high-repetition sets or when fatigued.
common_mistakes: Improper alignment and loss of postural control during high-repetition sets, particularly when fatigued or using a narrow base of support.
specific_findings: Jang et al. concluded that the choice between narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups should depend on the athlete’s specific needs, with narrow-based push-ups being better for triceps isolation and shoulder-width push-ups providing a more balanced upper-body workout (Jang et al., 2019)

An EMG study by Chen and Yu (2021) examined the muscle activation patterns of gymnastic athletes performing both push-up variations under fatigued and non-fatigued conditions... indicating that narrow-based push-ups were superior for triceps recruitment, even under fatigued conditions.

Chen and Yu (2021) highlighted that gymnasts displayed better postural control during shoulder-width push-ups due to the broader base of support, which reduced the risk of improper alignment during high-repetition sets

A study conducted by Muller et al. (2020) focused on the effects of narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups on upper-body endurance in adolescent gymnasts. The study employed a 10-week endurance training program...
Gymnasts who trained using narrow-based push-ups demonstrated greater fatigue resistance in the triceps and anterior deltoid (Muller et al., 2020).
Gymnasts who trained with shoulder-width push-ups displayed superior endurance in the pectoralis major and overall chest musculature (Muller et al., 2020).

Tanaka and Yamada (2022) found that narrow-based push-ups increased endurance in the stabilizing muscles of the shoulder, particularly the rotator cuff, while shoulder-width push-ups enhanced chest endurance.

core_principles: Incorporate both narrow-based and shoulder-width push-ups to achieve adequate muscle balance and reduce injury risk.
Use narrow-based push-ups to target the triceps and shoulder stabilizers (rotator cuff) to improve shoulder stability and aid in rehabilitation.
Use shoulder-width push-ups to engage the pectoralis major and anterior deltoids for balanced upper-body development.
Maintain a balance between variations to protect against overuse injuries such as rotator cuff strains, elbow tendinitis, and shoulder impingements.
common_mistakes: Over-reliance on a single push-up variation, which can lead to muscle imbalances and overuse injuries like rotator cuff strains or elbow tendinitis.
specific_findings: Lee et al. (2017) found that narrow-based push-ups improved shoulder stability by strengthening the triceps and rotator cuff muscles to maintain proper joint alignment during overhead movements.

Rodriguez and Mendes (2023) found that narrow-based push-ups were particularly effective in the rehabilitation phase for athletes with rotator cuff injuries, allowing strength rebuilding without premature shoulder joint overloading.
Kim et al. (2019) found that narrow-based push-ups significantly improved gymnasts' performance in planche progressions due to direct transfer of triceps activation to elbow extension.
Kim et al. (2019) found that shoulder-width push-ups benefited dynamic skills like vaults and ring swings where chest and shoulder strength are critical.

core_principles: For a standard shoulder-width push-up, place hands directly under the shoulder joints.
For a narrow-width push-up, place hands directly beneath the sternum.
Maintain an aligned body posture in a prone position with feet on the ground.
Control the repetition tempo, such as using a 2-second full cycle starting from the top position.
specific_findings: The study analyzed a single healthy male gymnastic participant (age: 25 years, weight: 65 kg).
The push-up cycle was standardized at a rate of 2 seconds per repetition starting from the top position.
The study compared narrow width push-up position (NWPP) directly beneath the sternum to shoulder width push-up position (SWPP) under the shoulder joint.
EMG signals were collected bilaterally from the pectoralis major (PM) and triceps brachii (T) muscles.

core_principles: Hand placement width significantly influences triceps brachii muscle activation and elbow joint kinematics.
Narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) elicit higher triceps brachii EMG activity compared to shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP).
Narrow-width push-ups restrict the elbow joint's range of motion compared to shoulder-width push-ups, which alters how load is developed on the elbow joint.
common_mistakes: Using an excessively narrow hand placement restricts the elbow range of motion, limiting the movement to between 154.45 and 118.23 degrees compared to a wider stance.
specific_findings: Triceps brachii EMG RMS value was 21.04 +/- 0.26 in NWPP compared to 19.97 +/- 0.39 in SWPP.
Average elbow joint angle was 139.81 degrees in SWPP and 135.22 degrees in NWPP.
Elbow range of motion (ROM) in SWPP/WWPP was 164.99 to 96.91 degrees.
Elbow range of motion (ROM) in NWPP was restricted to between 154.45 to 118.23 degrees.
The coefficient of correlation between joint angle alteration and EMG amplitude was 0.099 during NWPP (F=10.59) and 0.882 for SWPP.

core_principles: Narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) target the triceps more effectively and result in higher muscle activation compared to shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP).
Shoulder-width push-ups (SWPP) distribute the load more evenly between the shoulders and elbows, making them more suitable for general upper-body conditioning.
Narrow-width push-ups (NWPP) place greater strain on the elbow joint due to a deeper range of elbow movement (larger flexion angle).
common_mistakes: Using a narrow hand position (NWPP) when trying to minimize elbow joint strain or when seeking a balanced load distribution between the shoulders and elbows.
specific_findings: SWPP demonstrated an extension angle of 164.99 +/- 3.09 and a flexion angle of 96.91 +/- 6.20.
NWPP demonstrated a smaller extension angle of 154.45 +/- 3.96 but a larger flexion angle of 118.23 +/- 11.51.

core_principles: Use Narrow Width Push-ups (NWPP) to specifically target and isolate the triceps brachii.
Use Shoulder Width Push-ups (SWPP) to achieve a more balanced upper-body workout and better overall chest (pectoralis major) development.
Recognize that narrow hand placement increases the internal moment required at the elbow joint, leading to higher triceps motor unit recruitment.
specific_findings: The increased activation during NWPP is likely due to the greater internal moment required at the elbow joint, as observed in earlier studies.
Simpson and Drury (2018) indicated that SWPP may elicit more pectoralis major activity, supporting the notion that this variation is better for overall chest development.
